title: Mirabel and the Colony
premise: On the fringe colony of Mirabel, navigator Vesper Nystrom keeps to herself, tending a beacon whose original commissioning records were lost—and guarding the cryo-hold where her own backup copies sleep in stasis. When the colony's children begin dreaming the same dream, a signal Vesper realizes is coming from the backups themselves, she can no longer pretend she is only a caretaker. The dreams are a distress call: the backups are waking, and the only relay that can arbitrate their claim to identity sits at the edge of dead space, reachable only before the jump window closes. Racing a decaying signal and a colony that suddenly wants her gone, Vesper reaches the relay, merges the question of who she is with who they are, and chooses to wake them—not as replacements, but as family—returning to Mirabel as the first member of a family she never expected to have.
about_author: Lior Nakamura is a former maritime radio operator who turned to science fiction after a decade of listening to voices at the edge of signal range. They write quiet, character-driven stories about people who maintain things nobody else remembers are important.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She performs her solitary maintenance ritual on the Mirabel beacon, cataloging its inexplicable power draw and the hold of sleeping backups below. Establishes her deliberate invisibility in colony life. Emotional beat: loneliness worn as a discipline, the comfort of routines that ask nothing of her.

chapters.title: Children of the Same Sleep
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. At the colony market, she overhears children describing an identical dream—a corridor of blue light, a voice counting backward. She recognizes the corridor: it's the cryo-hold. Emotional beat: dread arriving quietly, the first crack in her carefully maintained distance.

chapters.title: Manifest of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She breaks her own rules and decrypts the hold's manifest: eleven backups, all bearing her genetic and neural signature, all flagged to an account that predates the colony's founding charter. Emotional beat: vertigo—the discovery that her anonymity was designed by someone else.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Is For
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with colony teacher Amara Okonkwo, who brings the dreaming children to the beacon on a field trip. Vesper watches a child press her hand to the hull and recite Vesper's own childhood address. Emotional beat: exposure—her hidden past surfacing in someone else's mouth.

chapters.title: The Counting Voice
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Night. The dream reaches her at last: the corridor, the backward count, and a name—hers, spoken in her own voice but younger. She realizes the backups are dreaming outward through the beacon. Emotional beat: terror and a shameful flicker of longing.

chapters.title: Colony Council, Closed Session
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. The council debates the dreams; a faction led by quartermaster Doss Havel wants the beacon shut down and 'the Nystrom problem' examined. Vesper, summoned, says almost nothing. Emotional beat: the colony's welcome curdling into scrutiny.

chapters.title: Eleven Doors
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She descends into the hold and walks the corridor from her dream, touching each pod. One pod's readout differs: its occupant's neural pattern diverged years ago and is still changing. Emotional beat: grief for a self she might have been, fear of what's waking.

chapters.title: Amara at the Airlock
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Amara confronts Vesper privately, not with suspicion but with an offer of help—and an admission that she, too, once arrived somewhere running from a name. Emotional beat: the first genuine connection; Vesper almost accepts it.

chapters.title: Signal Decay
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Instrument analysis shows the dreams are a decaying broadcast with a fixed endpoint: the jump window to the dead-space relay closes in nineteen days, after which the signal—and the arbitration rights it carries—expires forever. Emotional beat: the clock starting, choice disguised as necessity.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. The beacon's uplink is physically damaged; Havel's faction denies it, unconvincingly. Vesper can repair it, but the repair will broadcast the hold's existence to the whole colony. Emotional beat: betrayal, and the realization that hiding is no longer survivable.

chapters.title: Confession at the Water Reclamation Plant
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She tells Amara everything—the backups, the commissioning records, her suspicion that she was placed on Mirabel as a caretaker who was never meant to learn why. Emotional beat: the relief and terror of being fully known by one person.

chapters.title: The Diverged One
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The changing pod's occupant sends a direct, waking message through the beacon: a request, not a demand—'Let us argue our own case.' Vesper realizes the backups don't want to replace her; they want standing. Emotional beat: the enemy becoming a person.

chapters.title: Nineteen to Nine
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Preparations to fly Vesper's old survey ship to the relay. Havel moves to impound it; the dreaming children, unprompted, stage a quiet protest at the pad. Emotional beat: found family assembling itself before Vesper will admit she has one.

chapters.title: Departure Window
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She launches with Amara as copilot, leaving the beacon in the hands of the children's eldest, twelve-year-old Sef. The colony watches from the ridge. Emotional beat: leaving a place for the first time knowing she'll want to return.

chapters.title: Dead Space
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Transit through the silent reach where no beacon answers. The ship's long-range array picks up the relay still transmitting—but faintly, and something else is now answering it from deeper in the dark. Emotional beat: isolation with company, the vast indifference of space.

chapters.title: The Answering Dark
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. The second signal resolves: a corporate reclamation vessel, dispatched by whoever commissioned the beacon, coming to claim the backups as property before the window closes. Emotional beat: the past arriving as an adversary with paperwork.

chapters.title: Arbitration
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. They reach the relay with hours to spare. Vesper transmits her claim—and then, at the last moment, adds the backups' claim alongside her own, ceding them standing. The relay's ancient arbitration protocol accepts both. Emotional beat: the climax of identity—she wins by refusing to win alone.

chapters.title: The Reclamation
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. The corporate vessel arrives to find the arbitration sealed and legally binding: eleven persons, not property. Havel's sabotage is exposed in the transmitted record. The reclamation ship withdraws. Emotional beat: vindication that feels strangely hollow without the people it protects.

chapters.title: Wake Protocol
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She sends the wake command from the relay, then flies home through the closing window, unsure what she'll find. The eleven wake into a corridor that is, for the first time, dreaming outward with the lights on. Emotional beat: hope as an act of nerve.

chapters.title: Twelve at the Table
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. The backups arrive at Mirabel—not copies of Vesper, but people shaped by their own divergent decades of dormancy. The colony, led by the children, sets twelve places at the harvest table. Emotional beat: belonging offered before it is earned, and accepted.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Remembers
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She finally deciphers the beacon's original commissioning: her mother, a navigator who vanished in dead space, left it as a lighthouse for anyone the corporation might someday discard—including her. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into inheritance.

chapters.title: First Watch, Together
chapters.summary: Shared POV. One year later: the beacon maintained by rotation, the backups building lives, Sef teaching the younger children the maintenance ritual. Vesper takes the first watch, no longer alone, and the dream, when it comes now, is just a dream. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace; family as a thing you keep, like a light.
